      "id": 652233025,
      "created_at": "2026-05-04T20:50:32Z",
      "body": "$KOPN $AAOI $LITE $POET \n\nMassive Growth Potential for KOPN. 2 of the Top 5 Semiconductor interested with their AI optical interconnectivity:\n\nOPTICAL INTERCONNECT VS KOPN MICROLED\n\n1. Optical Interconnect (traditional)\n\nThis is the current standard in high-speed data systems.\n\nUses lasers (usually VCSELs or silicon photonics) to transmit data as light\n\nLight travels through optical fiber or waveguides\n\nCommon in:\n    * Data centers\n    * AI clusters (think NVIDIA GPUs)\n    * Telecom networks\n\nKey idea:\n\nConvert electrical \u2192 optical \u2192 electrical\n\nPros:\n\n* Very fast (Tbps scale)\n* Long distance capability\n* Mature ecosystem\n\nCons:\n\n* Power-hungry (especially conversions)\n* Expensive packaging\n* Heat + latency from multiple components\n\n2.  MicroLED Interconnect (emerging concept)\n\nThis is newer and more experimental.\n\n* Uses MicroLED arrays as the light source for data transmission\n* Instead of a laser, each tiny LED pixel can transmit data\n* Often paired with direct chip-to-chip or short-range optical links\n\nKey idea:\n\nUse massively parallel light emitters (MicroLED pixels) for communication\n\n3. Why MicroLED interconnect matters\n\nIt\u2019s trying to solve a growing bottleneck in AI systems:\n\n* Moving data is becoming more expensive than computing\n\n* Chips (GPUs, ASICs) are packed tightly \u2192 copper struggles\n\n* Optical helps, but lasers + packaging = costly\n\nMicroLED interconnect aims to:\n\n* Reduce power consumption\n* Enable short-range, ultra-dense data transfer\n* Potentially integrate directly onto chips",
      "username": "TheBullishTrade",
      "user_followers": 4967,
      "user_official": false,

      "created_at": "2026-05-04T16:58:48Z",
      "body": "$APP Adam Foroughi counters the \"SaaS is dead\" narrative by arguing that AI is actually the ultimate margin expander for software, transforming companies into hyper-efficient entities capable of generating massive revenue with minimal headcount. He posits that while AI might commoditize simple features, it cannot replicate the distribution power, proprietary data loops, and execution moats that established leaders possess. Foroughi views the shift away from per-seat pricing not as a death knell, but as an evolution toward outcome-based models where software captures more value by delivering direct results.       "body": "$AXTI $AXTX $COHR \nCoherent (COHR) does not manufacture the raw Indium Phosphide (InP) crystal substrates from scratch.       "id": 657213997,
      "created_at": "2026-06-23T18:04:45Z",
      "body": "$AAOI $AEHR $AXTI $OPTX $SOL.X \nA 6.4T optical engine uses more (InP) materials than a 3.2T optical engine.Why 6.4T Consumes More InP MaterialsThe primary driver behind InP material consumption is the total lane count and light source volume required to double the bandwidth from 3.2 Tbps to 6.4 Tbps:Lane Count Multiplication: To scale up to multi-terabit architectures, optical engines rely on multiplying physical lanes or laser wavelengths. A 6.4T engine requires twice the data-carrying capacity of a 3.2T engine. Even when transitioning to next-generation individual 400G-per-lane speeds, a 6.4T engine requires 16 channels, whereas a 3.2T engine requires only 8 channels.Laser Component Volume: Whether the architecture uses discrete InP Electro-absorption Modulated Lasers (EMLs) or continuous-wave (CW) InP lasers arrayed to feed a Silicon Photonics (SiPho) engine, the physical number of laser chips or array sizes must scale up to deliver the necessary optical power and channels.",
      "username": "graph",

      "id": 657124692,
      "created_at": "2026-06-22T23:41:17Z",
      "body": "$AXTI quantum computers need InP semiconductor materials!\n\nPhotonic Quantum Computers: InP is a foundational material here. Because InP has a direct bandgap, it is highly efficient at emitting and absorbing light. Many optical quantum chips use InP for on-chip lasers, optical modulators, and photodetectors to route and manipulate qubits encoded in photons.Superconducting Quantum Computers: These are the types of systems built by major players like IBM and Google, which use metals like aluminum or niobium for the actual qubits. However, they require massive arrays of classical electronic control hardware, switches, and microwave amplifiers to measure quantum states. Fast compound semiconductors, including InP, are essential for fabricating these cryogenic control chips and bridging the gap to classical hardware.",
      "username": "graph",
      "user_followers": 148,
      "user_official": false,
      "sentiment": "Bullish",
      "engagement": 0
    },

      "body": "$AXTI $NVDA $QMCO $RGTI \n\nHere\u2019s how they tie together:\n\n\ud83d\udd39 AI Data Centers Today\n\n* Powered mostly by GPUs from Nvidia, AMD, and custom chips.\n* Handle AI training, inference, cloud computing, and massive data storage.\n* Require enormous amounts of electricity, networking, and cooling.\n\n\ud83d\udd39 Quantum Computing Tomorrow\n\n* Won\u2019t replace AI data centers.\n* Will likely be connected to them as specialized accelerators, similar to how GPUs work alongside CPUs today.\n* Could solve certain optimization, simulation, chemistry, and cryptography problems exponentially faster than classical computers.\n\n\ud83d\udd39 AI + Quantum = Potential Synergy\n\nFuture AI data centers may contain:\n\n* CPUs\n* GPUs\n* AI accelerators\n* Quantum processors (QPUs)",

      "id": 657110561,
      "created_at": "2026-06-22T20:43:30Z",
      "body": "$AXTI A 6.4T optical engine uses more Indium Phosphide (InP) materials than a 3.2T optical engine.Why 6.4T Consumes More InP MaterialsThe primary driver behind InP material consumption is the total lane count and light source volume required to double the bandwidth from 3.2 Terabits per second  to 6.4 Tbps:Lane Count Multiplication: To scale up to multi-terabit architectures, optical engines rely on multiplying physical lanes or laser wavelengths. A 6.4T engine requires twice the data-carrying capacity of a 3.2T engine. Even when transitioning to next-generation individual 400G-per-lane speeds, a 6.4T engine requires 16 channels, whereas a 3.2T engine requires only 8 channels.Laser Component Volume: Whether the architecture uses discrete InP Electro-absorption Modulated Lasers (EMLs) or continuous-wave (CW) InP lasers arrayed to feed a Silicon Photonics (SiPho) engine, the physical number of laser chips or array sizes must scale up to deliver the necessary optical power and channels.",
      "username": "graph",

      "created_at": "2026-06-22T15:41:35Z",

      "body": "$VIST $CRDOON $CIEN $AXTI $VIAV\n\nArtificial intelligence has captured the market\u2019s attention, but the companies making headlines are only part of the story.       "id": 657026871,
      "created_at": "2026-06-22T11:20:37Z",
      "body": "Markets have been following a clear trajectory since the launch of ChatGPT and AI in late 2022, and that\u2019s rotating themes.\n\nThe Artificial Intelligence technological renaissance is the high level theme, driving a major bull market that likely lasts many more years.\n\nBut within that, we have seen many sub themes come and go.\n\nWe had NVDA lead the initial wave with compute and GPUs\u2026 obvious in hindsight that we needed immense amounts of compute to train these LLMs.\n\nThen came the power wave as we realized data centers needed immense electricity, names like CEG and VST soared, while spec names like OKLO and now BE followed suit. \n\nThen came the massive memory crunch, $MU, $SNDK and more got bid to the moon and keep going higher.\n\nPhotonics has been a major theme in recent months with the likes of $COHR  $AXTI and $LITE . \n\nThe next theme is bigger.\n\nBringing AI to the physical world.\n\n10 stocks for the robotics/automation trade:\n\nhttps://kryptonresearch.substack.com/p/the-iron-age",

      "id": 655527087,
      "created_at": "2026-06-05T13:03:12Z",
      "body": "$COST \n\nFinancial Strength: Costco currently holds a massive cash hoard of roughly $19 billion, including over $13 billion in net cash.Historical Precedent: Costco has historically issued debt every few years to fund large special payouts rather than completely depleting its own cash reserves.How to Monitor the Debt OfferingIf and when Costco decides to utilize this shelf registration, the specifics of the debt will be announced:The Amount: Analysts estimate a special dividend could result in a payout of roughly $13 billion, with the company funding $8 billion to $10 billion via this debt.Filing Details: You can track the exact types and quantities of securities offered on the Costco Investor Relations SEC Filings",
      "username": "jayjogia",
      "user_followers": 248,
      "user_official": false,
      "sentiment": "",
      "engagement": 0
    },
    {
      "id": 655527064,
      "created_at": "2026-06-05T13:03:01Z",
      "body": "$COST \n\nCostco filed an automatic shelf registration statement (Form S-3ASR) with the SEC on June 3, 2026. This type of filing allows the company to raise capital by issuing debt securities from time to time without needing to file new registration statements.Why the S-3 Filing MattersWhile the filing itself gives Costco the flexibility to issue debt for general corporate purposes, Wall Street analysts suspect a more specific motive.Potential Special Dividend: Analysts at Truist Securities speculate that the debt raise could be used to fund a massive special dividend for shareholders.",
      "username": "jayjogia",
      "user_followers": 248,
      "user_official": false,
      "sentiment": "",
      "engagement": 0
    },

      "body": "$COST \n\nThis is not true \n\nCostco (NASDAQ: COST) does not currently have a special dividend announced, having most recently paid a massive $12 per share special dividend on January 16, 2026.       "created_at": "2026-06-24T20:54:53Z",
      "body": "$MU is getting a lot more demand visibility through these $DRAM  take-or-pay contracts. \n \nFeels like memory is becoming less purely cyclical and more locked-in at scale. \n \nKey idea: \nCustomers commit to fixed volumes over multiple years \nTake-or-pay structure reduces demand uncertainty \nSignals tight supply-demand balance in AI memory \n \nWhy it matters: \nRevenue becomes more predictable \nDownside risk in cycles is partially cushioned \nAI demand is strong enough to justify long-term contracts \n \nSimple read: \nThis is no longer just spot market memory pricing \nIt\u2019s increasingly contract-driven demand \n \n$MU here feels closer to a structured demand business than a pure cycle chip name.",

      "created_at": "2026-06-11T01:54:14Z",
      "body": "Starbucks Corp. is exploring strategic options for its Japan business, including the potential sale of a stake, following its recent decision to sell a majority interest in its China operations, according to people familiar with the matter. The company has reportedly held preliminary discussions with investment banks to evaluate its strategy in one of its most important international markets, where it operates nearly 2,100 stores, most of them directly managed. \nSources said a stake sale could value the Japanese business at between \u00a5400 billion and \u00a5500 billion, potentially attracting interest from industry players and private equity firms. An initial public offering of the Japan unit is also being considered, although no final decisions have been made. \nThe move would align with Starbucks' broader strategy of adopting more asset-light partnerships outside the U.S. to support growth while freeing up capital for investments in its brand, product innovation, and digital capabilities. \n$SBUX",

      "id": 655928269,
      "created_at": "2026-06-09T20:22:19Z",
      "body": "Starbucks could double its international store count over time, CEO Brian Niccol said Tuesday at the Evercore Consumer & Retail Conference, signaling a long-term expansion strategy focused on global growth. \nThe company currently operates around 22,000 stores outside the U.S., and Niccol said there is no fundamental reason that figure cannot eventually double, highlighting continued demand and brand strength in international markets. \nIn the U.S., he added that Starbucks also has room to add at least 5,000 additional locations, with particular opportunities in underpenetrated regions between Texas and Virginia as well as across the broader Midwest. Niccol noted the company has historically been concentrated on the West and East Coasts, leaving \u201cnot enough presence in the middle of the country.\u201d \nStarbucks operates more than 41,000 stores across 89 global markets, including company-operated and licensed locations, with roughly 23,000 stores outside the U.S. and Canada. \n$SBUX",
      "username": "topstockalerts",

      "id": 655724106,
      "created_at": "2026-06-08T12:01:10Z",
      "body": "$SRAD \n\nSportradar and Kalshi Announce First-of-its-Kind Data and Infrastructure Global Partnership for Prediction Markets\n\nMonday, 8th June at 8:00 am\n-Global Agreement Positions Sportradar as Core Data and Solutions Provider Across Premier Sports Leagues-\n\n--Opportunity to participate across Kalshi ecosystem including market makers and brokers--\n\nST. GALLEN, Switzerland and NEW YORK, June 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sportradar Group AG (NASDAQ: SRAD) today announced a landmark multi-year global agreement with Kalshi, the world's largest prediction market. This strategic agreement positions Sportradar as an official data and solutions provider for Kalshi, delivering a broad portfolio of premium sports content and services across major sports properties including Major League Baseball (MLB), the National Hockey League (NHL), Major League Soccer (MLS), and Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), among others.\n\nAs prediction markets continue to emerge as a fast growing and regulated segment of the sports ecosystem, Sportradar is positioned to play a foundational role in enabling their growth and facilitating a framework for integrity. This agreement also establishes the ability for Sportradar to enter into agreements directly with Kalshi's key partners, including brokers and market makers, with real time official data and scalable solutions across the value chain.\n\nSportradar will provide Kalshi with a range of solutions from Sportradar Prediction Services, including:\n\nOfficial Sports Data and Live Odds: Fast, reliable, accurate official data and live odds to power pre-game and in-play markets, enhancing market efficiency while ensuring timely settlements\nFan Engagement Solutions: Dynamic, real-time content, including scores, schedules, and data visualizations, designed to drive deeper engagement\nCustomer Acquisition Solutions: Leading marketing services to help acquire high value sports fans\nIndustry-Leading Integrity Services: Robust integrity framework including Sportradar UFDS AI, which detects suspicious behavior, and Sportradar Integrity Exchange (SIE), which enables participants to share integrity threats through a secure network",
      "username": "TheBullishTrade",
      "user_followers": 5742,
      "user_official": false,
      "sentiment": "",
      "engagement": 0
    },

      "body": "$TMDX  \nClaude: \nPractical read on the next 90 days.       "created_at": "2026-07-06T13:26:31Z",

      "created_at": "2026-07-05T14:21:45Z",
      "body": "$MU $SNDK $WDC $MRVL  People need to forget about this industry as being cyclical anymore. It's not. Today's demands are not the same as before. AI didn't exist before.
